```{r library setup}

library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot2movies)
```


[link to the description online](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/ggplot2movies/movies.html)

The data contains:
- 58,788 movies (rows)
- 24 columns: 
  - Movie title 
  - Year
  - Length (minutes)
  - Budget
  - Rating
  - Votes
  - r1-10 (percentile per score 1-10, rounded to nearest 10%)
  - MPAA rating
  - Genre (action, animation, comedy, drama, documentary, romance, short)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot2movies)
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
```

# Plot 1

*the ranking of the movies (points) by year and colored by their genre*

```{r}
genre_levels <- c("NA", "0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6")

genre_labels <- c(
  "NA",
  "Crosslisted",
  "Action",
  "Animation",
  "Comedy",
  "Drama",
  "Documentary",
  "Romance"
  )

genre_colors <- c(
  "grey",
  "chartreuse4",
  "gold",
  "blue",
  "orange",
  "mediumpurple",
  "hotpink",
  "violetred4"
  )


plot1 <- clean_movies|> 
  mutate(genre = fct_na_value_to_level(
      factor(genre, levels = genre_levels),
      level = "NA")) |>
  filter(votes >= 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = rating, color = genre, fill = genre)) + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(breaks = genre_levels, 
                    labels = genre_labels,
                    values = genre_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(breaks = genre_levels, 
                    labels = genre_labels,
                    values = genre_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(11890, 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, 1940,1950,1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1:10)) +
=======
sum(is.na(movies$year)) # no missing values
sum(is.na(movies$rating))

# genre assignment with accounting for multiple assignments per movie
genres <- c("Action", "Animation", "Comedy", "Drama", "Documentary", "Romance")

clean_movies <- movies |>
  select(-budget, -mpaa) |>
  mutate(
    genre_combo = apply(
      pick(all_of(genres)), 1,
      \(x) paste(genres[as.logical(x)], collapse = " + ")
    ),
    genre = factor(ifelse(genre_combo == "", "None", genre_combo))
  )

# finding the highest and lowest rated movies on IMDB and their statistics

highest <- filter(clean_movies, rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest)
lowest  <- filter(clean_movies, rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest)

highest_table <- clean_movies |> filter(clean_movies, rating == max(rating)) |>
  select(title, year, rating, votes, genre, length) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Highest rated movies on IMDB") |>
  cols_label(
    title = "Title",
    year  = "Year",
    rating = "Rating (1-10)",
    votes = "Votes",
    genre = "Genre",
    length = "Length (min)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = votes, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = rating, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Data from ggplot2's movies dataset.",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  )

highest_table

lowest_table <- lowest |>

# They have very few votes, thus I made other versions with votes above 100 and 1000
highest100 <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 100) |> filter(rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest100)
lowest100  <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 100) |> filter(rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest100)

cat(str_glue(
  "Highest rated movie when filtering for more than 100 votes: \n {highest100$title} ({highest100$year})\n",
  "  Genre: {highest100$genre}\n",
  "  Rating: {highest100$rating} from {highest100$votes} votes\n\n",
  "Lowest rated movie when filtering for more than 100 votes:  \n {lowest100$title} ({lowest100$year})\n",
  "  Genre: {lowest100$genre}\n",
  "  Rating: {lowest100$rating} from {lowest100$votes} votes"
))
# function for cleanliness and robustness to multiple movies with the same rating instead: 
print_movies <- function(movies_df) {
  str_glue_data(movies_df,
    "{title} ({year})\n",
    "  Genre: {genre}\n",
    "  Rating: {rating} from {votes} votes\n"
  )
}

print_group <- function(label, movies_df) {
  cat(str_glue("\n{label}:\n\n",
               str_c(print_movies(movies_df), collapse = "\n\n")))
}

highest1000 <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 1000) |> filter(rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest1000)
lowest1000  <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 1000) |> filter(rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest1000)


print_group("Highest rated movies when filtering for more than 1000 votes", highest1000)
print_group("Lowest rated movies when filtering for more than 1000 votes", lowest1000)

# Overview Table by Genre
```{r genre table}

table(factor(clean_movies$genre))  # basic table

genre_table <- clean_movies |>
  filter(votes > 20) |>
  group_by(genre) |>
  summarise(
    n_movies     = n(),
    n_votes      = sum(votes),
    avg_rating   = mean(rating),
    wtd_rating   = sum(votes * rating) / n_votes) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Genre representation of movies on IMDB"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    genre       = "Genre / genre combination",
    n_movies    = "Number of movies",
    n_votes     = "Total number of votes",
    avg_rating  = "Average rating",
    wtd_rating  = "Vote-weighted rating"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(n_movies, n_votes),
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(avg_rating, wtd_rating),
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Data from ggplot2's movies dataset.",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  )

genre_table

```{r}
# already above, but repeated for clarity
genres <- c("Action", "Animation", "Comedy", "Drama", "Documentary", "Romance")

pair_levels <- apply(combn(genres, 2), 2, \(p) paste(p, collapse = " + "))
# "Action + Animation", "Action + Comedy", ..., "Documentary + Romance"

genre_levels <- c("None", "Unknown", "Crosslisted",
                  genres, pair_levels)          # 9 + 15 = 24 levels

genre_labels <- c("No genre", "Unknown", "Crosslisted (3+)",
                  genres, pair_levels)

# the base colors, get combined later
genre_colors <- c(
  None         = "grey50",
  Unknown      = "grey",
  Crosslisted  = "chartreuse4",
  Action       = "gold",
  Animation    = "blue",
  Comedy       = "orange",
  Drama        = "mediumpurple",
  Documentary  = "hotpink",
  Romance      = "violetred4"
)

clean_movies <- clean_movies |>
  mutate(
    n_genres = rowSums(pick(all_of(genres))),
    genre = case_when(
      is.na(n_genres) ~ "Unknown",
      n_genres == 0   ~ "None",
      n_genres >= 3   ~ "Crosslisted",
      TRUE            ~ genre_combo      # exact match for singles AND pairs
    ) |>
      factor(levels = genre_levels)
  )

dual_genre <- clean_movies |>
  filter(votes >= 100) |>
  mutate(
    parts = str_split(genre, " \\+ "),
    genre_left  = map_chr(parts, 1),
    genre_right = map_chr(parts, \(p) if (length(p) == 2) p[2] else NA_character_) |>
              coalesce(genre_left) # makes single genres a full colored circle
  )

plot1 <- dual_genre |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = rating,
             colour = genre_left, fill = genre_right)) +
  halfmoon(alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = base_colors, name = "Genre (right)") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = base_colors, name = "Genre (left)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, 1940,
                                1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
